question: When was International Anti-Corruption Day Celebrated in 2021 (an annual event) to raise awareness and find newer ways to combat corruption?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mon Dec 09 2024 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• International Anti-Corruption Day is observed on **December 9th** each year.

• This day was designated by the **United Nations General Assembly** in 2003.

• The purpose of this day is to raise public awareness about the dangers of corruption and the need to combat it.

• Various events and activities are organized worldwide on this day to promote anti-corruption measures and policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC)**

• The UNCAC is the only legally binding international anti-corruption multilateral treaty.

• It was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on October 31, 2003, and entered into force in December 2005.

• It covers a wide range of corruption-related issues, including prevention, criminalization, international cooperation, and asset recovery.

• The convention promotes measures to prevent and combat corruption more effectively.

• **Transparency International**

• Transparency International is a global civil society organization that leads the fight against corruption.

• It was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Berlin, Germany.

• Transparency International publishes the annual Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI), which ranks countries by their perceived levels of public sector corruption.

• The organization's mission is to create change towards a world free of corruption.

• **Global Anti-Corruption Initiatives**

• Many international and regional organizations work towards combating corruption, including the World Bank, International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

• These organizations provide technical assistance, policy advice, and funding for anti-corruption programs in various countries.

• Anti-corruption initiatives often focus on promoting transparency, accountability, and good governance.

• Collaboration between governments, civil society, and the private sector is crucial in the fight against corruption.
